topic: The moment Elvis realized his career was in danger — and what he did about it
script: For more than seven years, Elvis Presley did not give a single live concert. After a benefit show at Pearl Harbor in March 1961, he turned to Hollywood. The films kept coming. By 1968, the box office was fading, and his career needed mending. Then, in June, he walked into NBC's studios in Burbank, California. Director Steve Binder did not want a Christmas special. He wanted something raw, something for a younger audience. So Elvis stepped onto a small stage in black leather, surrounded by trusted musicians and a live crowd. It was his first concert since that night in Hawaii. On December 3, 1968, NBC broadcast the result. It drew forty-two percent of the television audience, the most-watched show of its season. He closed in a white suit, singing a new song, If I Can Dream. Seven years of silence. One night of television. The King was back.
